response.sql: SELECT AVG(rebrate / feerate) AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees WHERE feerate >= 0.0009 AND feerate IS NOT NULL AND rebrate IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: The high fee-rate band is inclusive of the cutoff (feerate >= 0.0009). The request does not say whether 0.0009 itself belongs to the band.
Records with a NULL feerate or NULL rebrate are excluded, so the count covers only records that contribute to the average. The ratio is averaged per record, not computed as a ratio of totals.

rebrate and feerate are stored on the same fractional scale (for example 0.00015 and 0.00050, as the documentation shows), so their quotient is meaningful. Because feerate is at least 0.0009, the division cannot hit zero.

alternatives.interpretation: The high band is strictly above the cutoff, so records with feerate exactly equal to 0.0009 are excluded.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(rebrate / feerate) AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees WHERE feerate > 0.0009 AND feerate IS NOT NULL AND rebrate IS NOT NULL;
